hypothesis: Independent five-second goal-offset noise may yield smaller physical heading deviations than temporally persistent noise because of aircraft turn dynamics and repeated recentering.
controls: Identical two scenarios, untrained neutral actor, original dynamics and scorer, fixed route/static support, traffic filter off. Noise draws are shared by aircraft slot and decision.
held_noise_scope: Only heading noise is held for twelve decisions (60 simulated seconds). Speed noise remains independent and identical to iid020 for the same world/decision/aircraft.
primary_diagnostics: Latent heading offset standard deviation and within-aircraft lag-one correlation.
Actual turn RMS and route-reference drift RMS, with filter intervention and command saturation reported.
Original physical metrics shown only as descriptive consequences on these two reused worlds.
limitations: No PPO training and no learned-policy claim.
Temporal holding is an actuation probe, not a valid drop-in on-policy sampling method.
Only two previously used development worlds; this cannot justify a performance ranking.
Static support can change commands; intervention rates are recorded.
Terminal aircraft removed before step returns have no post-step simulator heading.
next_action: Use measured response to decide whether a properly specified temporal exploration method warrants a separate matched RL experiment. Do not infer learning from this diagnostic.
preservation: No model, source bundle, classical controller or active experiment is changed.
previous_attempt: runs/exploration-actuation-diagnostic-v1: startup failed before any scenarios ran because the simulator work directory did not exist; all files retained.
